$comment: The boundary list. This file is the specification of what the drill proves;
the harness is generic. Add a boundary here, not in drill.py.
Each row: which window to catch the pipeline inside (window, a named predicate
over the spool snapshot), what the lake does to it (lake: ack | drop | dead),
the knobs that widen the window (env), the same knobs relaxed for the restart
(restart_env), the records the drill appends before and after the kill, and
what the merged lake export must hold afterwards (expect).

boundaries.name: post-emit-pre-batch
boundaries.claim: the cursor already covers the lines the batcher still holds in memory, so the kill loses exactly that batch and duplicates none of it: stated loss, no duplicate work

boundaries.name: post-batch-pre-send
boundaries.claim: the receipt's bytes were published before the receipt existed, so the receipt survives the kill and the restart ships the whole backlog: zero loss

boundaries.name: post-batch-pre-send@mid-write
boundaries.claim: a kill inside the write itself leaves no torn bundle at a published path and no receipt without whole bytes; the half-written bytes are invisible and the restart re-reads nothing it cannot prove

boundaries.name: post-send-pre-ack
boundaries.claim: an upload the lake accepted and dropped acks nothing, so the receipt stays pending through the kill and the same bytes ship once after the restart

boundaries.name: post-ack-pre-cursor
boundaries.claim: an ack the pipeline received but never committed replays a bundle the lake already holds; the lake absorbs the replay by digest, so the export is still exactly once
